tier_reason: Every quoted number matches site/data/results/cutelyst.json and the sibling drogon/express/flask/django.json files in MDA2AV/HttpArena; the benchmark code is public (frameworks/cutelyst/{Dockerfile,CMakeLists.txt,main.cpp,root.cpp,app.cpp}, frameworks/drogon/{Dockerfile,main.cc}, scripts/benchmark.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh), both entries build with CMake Release, and the CPU model (Threadripper PRO 3995WX) is in site/data/current.json, so tier A holds as for wtx on the same harness. The verdict is a downgrade of the claim, not of the tier: the async 5.3x row is an artifact of the Drogon entry's code, and the category's listed incumbents on the same board (nginx, actix-web) beat Cutelyst on the main profiles.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Against Drogon on HttpArena (all ratios derived from page data): baseline-4096 2,153,860 vs 2,022,710 req/s (1.06x); limited-conn-4096 1,736,401 vs 1,694,883 (1.02x); json-tls-4096 326,846 vs 253,055 (1.29x); pipelined-4096 (reference-only profile) 10,167,331 vs 7,801,404 (1.30x); async-32000 761,563 vs 143,001 (5.3x, but the Drogon entry runs every delay timer on its single main loop, so this row measures the entry, not Drogon). Against slower stacks on baseline-4096: Express 525,879 (4.1x), Flask 77,319 (27.9x), Django 29,206 (73.7x). The category's listed incumbents on the same board are faster: baseline-4096 nginx 3,284,513 and actix 2,775,120 req/s (Cutelyst 0.66x and 0.78x), json-tls-4096 nginx 1,313,755 and actix 1,157,219 (Cutelyst 0.25x and 0.28x), async-32000 actix 2,112,168 (0.36x); Cutelyst beats actix only on limited-conn-4096 (1,736,401 vs 1,135,157, 1.53x) and beats nginx only on pipelined-4096 (10,167,331 vs 4,037,345, 2.5x).
corrections.baseline: Drogon (C++ web framework, HttpArena's maintainer-written Drogon entry); the same results directory also holds Express, Flask and Django rows, and the listed incumbents nginx and actix-web, which beat Cutelyst on baseline-4096 and json-tls-4096
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Cutelyst: g++ from the ubuntu:26.04 image (version not stated), C++23, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release with no extra flags, Ninja; Cutelyst built from upstream commit 5ec5ce95d80a87b38ea45a326945bb22e515a23a (its libraries overlaid on the v5.1.0 .deb in the runtime image), Qt 6 from Ubuntu, Cutelee v6.2.0, ASql commit eebafdde (frameworks/cutelyst/Dockerfile and CMakeLists.txt in MDA2AV/HttpArena). Drogon: built on the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image (per drogon's docker/ubuntu/Dockerfile: Ubuntu 22.04, g++-11, Drogon master at image build time built by build.sh with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=release), app built with CMake Release, C++20, and libjemalloc preloaded (frameworks/drogon/Dockerfile).
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-Cores (128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 host, kernel 6.17.0-22, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), performance governor (site/data/current.json); per scripts/lib/profiles.sh the server container is pinned to cpuset 0-31,64-95 (32 physical cores plus SMT siblings) and the load generator runs on the remaining CPUs of the same machine.
corrections.workload: HttpArena HTTP/1.1 profiles, each the best of three 5 s runs (scripts/benchmark.sh) with the gcannon load generator: baseline (mixed GET/POST /baseline11 summing query parameters and body, 4096 connections), limited-conn (same, connections closed after 10 requests), pipelined (16x pipelining, reference-only and excluded from the composite score), json-tls (JSON serialization over HTTP/1.1 TLS, 4096 connections) and async (GET /delay/10, a flat 10 ms timer over 32,000 held connections, ceiling 3.2M req/s).
corrections.caveats: Margins over Drogon on the scored throughput profiles are small (1.06x baseline, 1.02x limited-conn) from best-of-three 5 s runs with no variance reported. The async 5.3x row is not evidence about Drogon: HttpArena's Drogon entry (frameworks/drogon/main.cc) schedules each delay with app().getLoop()->runAfter, the main event loop, so all 32,000 timers fire on one thread (Drogon CPU 812% vs Cutelyst 6172%), while Cutelyst's entry uses a per-worker QTimer. Pipelined is a reference-only profile. The runs are weeks apart: all Cutelyst rows were saved on 2026-10-06 (PR #1520), Drogon's rows were last saved on 2026-09-06 (PRs #1455 and #1460) on an unpinned drogon:latest image built with g++-11, so compiler generation and harness state differ between the two rows. The category's listed incumbents on the same board are faster: nginx 3,284,513 and actix 2,775,120 req/s vs Cutelyst 2,153,860 on baseline-4096; nginx 1,313,755, h2o 1,229,462 and actix 1,157,219 vs 326,846 on json-tls-4096; actix 2,112,168 vs 761,563 on async-32000; nginx 2,626,297 vs 1,736,401 on limited-conn-4096. Drogon beats Cutelyst on latency-500k-8cpu (374,962 vs 329,347 req/s), on mean latency and CPU in latency-1m (108.1 us vs 137.6 us, 3551.7% vs 3825.6%) and in 8gbit-512 (102.5 us vs 120.5 us, 304.0% vs 342.7%). Express beats Cutelyst on json-tls-4096 (394,866 vs 326,846 req/s). Cutelyst's database profiles are very weak: async-db-1024 and fortunes-1024 both reached 384 req/s with 2.0-2.3 s mean latency and 22-43% CPU (Express 173,099 and 58,855), which looks like a stall in its per-thread ASql pool (about 3 connections per worker thread), so Cutelyst does not win on database or template workloads. The entry was written by Cutelyst's own author (meta.json maintainers: dantti, PRs #1479 and #1520), and its Dockerfile pins an upstream commit (2026-09-11, 'Add http chunked for HttpArena benchmarks') that adds chunked request bodies for this benchmark. The live leaderboard (www.http-arena.com) is blocked here and rankings may have changed. The Cutelyst README links HttpArena and historical TechEmpower Round 23 results but quotes no numbers.

notes: Numbers and ratios versus Drogon, Express, Flask and Django are exact, and license (BSD-3-Clause), 977 stars, last commit 2026-09-11 (not a fork, not archived) are confirmed, so tier A stays; the claim is downgraded because the async 5.3x win comes from the Drogon entry scheduling every timer on its main loop, Drogon's rows are a month older and built on an unpinned g++-11 image, and the category's listed incumbents nginx and actix-web on the same board beat Cutelyst on baseline-4096, json-tls-4096 and async. Record shortcomings: not faster than nginx or actix-web; only 1.02-1.06x over Drogon on scored throughput profiles; database and template profiles stall at 384 req/s; entry written by Cutelyst's author with a benchmark-specific upstream commit. The record's 'single 5 s runs' was corrected to best of three 5 s runs.
